items.title: El Pesero: el primer chiringuito playero de la historia emergió de un naufragio en Cádiz en 1752
items.description: Bautista Pesero era un tipo bien listo y un buen cocinero, es lo poco que se puede leer entre líneas del escaso rastro de migas de pan que la historia ha legado sobre él. Allá por febrero de 1752, le ficharon para cocinar en el campamento creado en la playa de Chiclana de la Frontera para rescatar los restos del trágico naufragio del Soberbio , un navío mercante. A Pesero le impusieron el precio máximo del menú que debía cobrar por alimentar a los 200 hombres desplegados para recuperar el oro, la plata y las monedas hundidas bajo el mar. Pero nada le dijeron de que, junto a esa barraca de madera construida con los restos del mismo hundimiento, crease otra, sin topes de precios, para alimentar a la multitud de curiosos que se asomaban por la actual playa de La Barrosa. Y así fue como este vecino gaditano del siglo XVIII se convirtió —por ahora— en el primer dueño documentado de un chiringuito en la costa española . Seguir leyendo

items.title: SGF mum as fake agency boss fires back
items.description: ***Says ‘you’ve been blind for 16 years’ ***Anambra SSG clarifies involvement in ‘fake’ federal agency By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — Embattled National Coordinator and Executive Director of the Made-in-Nigeria Project Office, an agency which existence is now under investigation, Nwabueze Buchi George, has dismissed growing public scrutiny of his organisation, telling critics that only their own lack of awareness could explain why they were just discovering a programme that had existed for 16 years. This was even as officials of the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, OSGF, declined to comment on the controversy trailing the outfit. Nwabueze’s comment, posted on LinkedIn in reaction to questions trailing his outfit, amid the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission’s clampdown on the National Brands Development and Made-in-Nigeria Special Project Office, described the scrutiny as a failure of observation rather than a legitimate query about the agency’s status. “How can you discover a 16 years program in 2026, it’s means you have been blind, we are committed to the national development,” he wrote. The remark followed a series of posts in which Nwabueze had traced the origin of his outfit to a June 15, 2010 initiative, presenting a letter from the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, dated July 19, 2010, as part of that history. That letter, however, was addressed to a “Buchi George” of The Hats Centre in Owerri, Imo State, and concerned the endorsement of a project, titled “Made In Naija” for an event in Ireland, rather than any Made-in-Nigeria brand development scheme. His claim of 16 years of continuous operation also runs against a separate document he posted, an appointment letter from the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation dated October 3, 2025, which formally conveyed his appointment as National Coordinator/Executive Director of the Made in Nigeria Project Office under a five-year tenure that began in July 2025. Materials Nwabueze has circulated to promote the office described it as an initiative to “Drive Local Production Development” under an “Industrialise Nigeria” campaign. The Made in Nigeria Project Office has come under scrutiny, following the ICPC’s investigation into what it describes as a fraudulent federal agency operating under a similar name, with questions raised over the legal basis, funding, and oversight of Nwabueze’s outfit within the Office of the SGF. Efforts by Vanguard to get the OSGF’s position on the matter proved abortive, as the Special Adviser on Media and Publicity to the Secretary to the Government of the Federation SGF, Yomi Odunuga, did not respond to enquiries, while the Head, Information and Public Relations at the OSGF, Chris Ugbuegbulam, was unreachable. With the OSGF’s silence leaving the questions unanswered, the legal basis, funding, and oversight of Nwabueze’s outfit within the presidency remain in the realm of speculation. However, a review of the Made in Nigeria Project Office’s website showed the portraits of 20 state coordinators, including those of Kogi, Bauchi, Oyo, Taraba, Kano, Ondo, Benue, Nasarawa, Plateau, Kaduna, Katsina, Niger, Zamfara, Abia, Sokoto, Ogun, Anambra, Osun, Kebbi, and Delta. Anambra SSG clarifies involvement in ‘fake’ federal agency Clarifying her involvement in the activities of the fake agency weekend, the Secretary to Anambra State Government, SSG, Chiamaka Nnake, said the office was planning to organise a Made-in-Nigeria fair in the state after she was nominated as the “focal person” for Anambra State. She said following the nominations, “focal persons” from the 36 states had been in a WhatsApp group discussing issues relating to the activities of the office. In a statement she released late on Saturday, Nnake said the office wrote to the state requesting that Anambra should host the South-East Made-in-Nigeria Fair. The statement read: “I wish to clarify the circumstances surrounding the trending news concerning the purported ‘Made-in-Nigeria Agency’, in which my photograph has been displayed and I have been identified as one of the state coordinators. “In January 2026, the governor received a letter from the Made-in-Nigeria Office, said to be under the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, requesting the nomination of a State Focal Person. “In response, the governor, in February 2026, nominated me as the state focal person for Anambra State. “Following the nominations, focal persons from the 36 states have been in a WhatsApp group engaging on issues relating to the activities of the office. “More recently, the same office wrote to the state requesting that Anambra host the South-East Made-in-Nigeria Fair. “The request was approved, and an inaugural meeting was held about two weeks ago, with the national coordinator in attendance.” According to her, the state committee has since been working on preparations for the fair, which was scheduled to take place from December 2 to 5, 2026. “Beyond these official interactions and engagements, she has no knowledge of, involvement in, or connection with any other activities, claims, or developments attributed to the said office. “I therefore wish to make it clear that anything beyond the above-mentioned official interactions is entirely outside my knowledge and involvement,” she added. Bureaucratic weaknesses allowed fraud to thrive – Ex-perm sec Meanwhile, former Permanent Secretary of the Federal Civil Service Commission, Goke Adeboroye, yesterday identified weaknesses in Nigeria’s bureaucratic system as reason for penetration of the government by an alleged fake presidential agency. Adeboroye spoke on Channels Television’s Inside Sources, posted on YouTube yesterday, following the discovery by the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission of the alleged Presidential Foreign Intervention Promotion Council, which the commission said operated with forged appointment letters and other official documents. He said the incident raised questions about how an individual could allegedly gain entry into the government system, secure an appointment, access budgetary provisions and obtain office space without the relevant authorities detecting the irregularities. “The exposure of that fake presidential agency is a major lapse to say that somebody can actually come into the system, get in on the budget, get offices, and all of that,” he said. Adeboroye identified weaknesses in the bureaucratic capacity of key offices within the Presidency and government, including the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, the Office of the Chief of Staff to the President and the Office of the Head of the Civil Service. He said the bureaucracy supporting these offices must be sufficiently capable of helping the President implement his policies while providing the necessary checks to prevent fraudulent or unlawful directives from taking effect. “The bureaucracy in those offices are not strong enough to be able to help the President drive the vision at the speed and with the efficiency that he wants,” Adeboroye said. He said the incident also highlighted the relationship between political office holders and career civil servants. He noted that while political appointees issue directives, civil servants must have the professional competence and integrity to question instructions that do not conform with established procedures. “The political office holders are principals to the bureaucracy, and a lot of times, the bureaucracy takes directives from them. “You need a bureaucracy that is not just professional but also has the capacity. The commitment to the system is also driven by his own or her own personal integrity,” he said. Adeboroye said civil servants should be able to identify suspicious communications purportedly originating from the Presidency because they are familiar with the established channels through which presidential approvals are transmitted. “Whether the person brings fake or whatever, you as the civil servant should be trained to be able to detect what should be a genuine communication from the State House. You work in that system,” he said. He explained that presidential approvals ordinarily pass through established channels involving senior government officials. “When the President approves anything, he always minutes to about three people. He goes to the Chief of Staff, he goes to SGF, and if he has something to do with civil service, the Head of Service will have it.” According to him, the existence of such channels should enable officials to verify questionable directives before acting on them. Adeboroye recalled an incident from his time as Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Interior involving a former governor who claimed to have presidential approval for a diplomatic passport. He said the then Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Immigration Service, Ude, did not act immediately but cross-checked the purported approval before proceeding. Adeboroye said the official discovered that there was indeed an approval but sought an audience to advise the President on whether the former governor, who was no longer in office, should be granted a diplomatic passport. He said the official’s action demonstrated the importance of experience and knowledge of government procedures in preventing irregularities. “That’s somebody using the experience of the system to ensure that you are not outplayed,” he said. Adeboroye added that officials could have easily verified the authenticity of questionable directives through direct communication with the relevant offices. “So we would have expected that on a simple phone call, when I was working in the office of Ekaette, Secretary of Government, I could pick a phone, call any minister, call this, it’s just a phone call from the office of whoever to say, ‘Chief of Staff, is this true’? And that would have actually corrected it,” he said. The post SGF mum as fake agency boss fires back appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Burkina Faso: Qui a « tué » l’inspecteur Rock de la série télévisée « Commissariat de Tampy » ?
items.description: Une onde de choc a brièvement secoué la communauté des cinéphiles burkinabè ce dimanche 23 août 2026 . Une publication devenue virale sur les réseaux sociaux annonçait avec gravité le décès tragique de Sekou Oumar Sidibe , l’emblématique interprète de l'inspecteur Rock dans la série culte « Commissariat de Tampy » , prétendument abattu lors d'un braquage à son domicile. Mais que les fans se rassurent : l'acteur est bel et bien vivant. Il s'agit d'une sordide campagne de désinformation menée par un internaute en quête de visibilité, contre lequel l'artiste compte désormais engager des poursuites judiciaires. Une onde de choc a brièvement secoué la communauté des cinéphiles burkinabè et ouest-africains ce dimanche 23 août 2026 . Une publication devenue virale sur les réseaux sociaux annonçait le décès de Sidibé Sékou Oumar , alias « l'inspecteur Roch », célèbre figure de la série culte « Commissariat de Tampy » , prétendument abattu lors d'un braquage à son domicile. Heureusement, l'acteur est bel et bien vivant. Derrière cette fausse nouvelle macabre se cache une simple tentative de manipulation d'audience en ligne, contre laquelle le comédien compte désormais engager des poursuites judiciaires. La rumeur s'est propagée à une vitesse fulgurante sur Facebook. Un visuel arborant le logo de « FADIMA WEBTV », publié par un internaute sous le pseudonyme de « L’INVISIBLE ✨ », annonçait brutalement la mort du célèbre comédien. Le message, accompagné de la mention tragique « RIP l'acteur Rock du Commissariat de Tampy, suite à un braquage à domicile, il a été tué par des criminels » , affirmait que le drame s'était produit ce dimanche 23 août 2026. Une annonce sordide qui a jeté le trouble au sein de sa communauté avant que l'intéressé ne rétablisse la vérité. Sidibé Sékou Oumar, plus connu sous le pseudonyme de « l'inspecteur Roch », est une figure incontournable du paysage de la fiction ouest-africaine. Il doit sa grande notoriété à son rôle d'inspecteur de police dans la série à succès « Commissariat de Tampy » . Créée et réalisée par le réalisateur burkinabè Missa Hébié en 2006 , cette œuvre emblématique est aujourd'hui considérée comme la toute première série policière humoristique de l'Afrique de l'Ouest. Grâce à son ton unique mêlant enquêtes criminelles burlesques et humour de proximité, elle a marqué des générations de téléspectateurs à travers tout le continent. « Bien vivant, en chair et en os » Face à l'inquiétude grandissante de ses proches et de ses nombreux fans, l'acteur est promptement sorti de son silence pour démentir catégoriquement la rumeur. « Je suis là, bien vivant en chair et en os ce jour 23 Août 2026 » , a rassuré Sidibé Sékou Oumar. Un soulagement immense pour ses admirateurs qui ont craint le pire pour celui qui a si longtemps incarné la loi et la sagacité à l'écran. Pour le comédien, le mobile de cette mise en scène de mauvais goût est évident : la quête effrénée d’audience sur internet. « Un individu a fait un truc pour avoir de la visibilité, je pense, avec cette affiche » , a-t-il réagi. Cette méthode, de plus en plus dénoncée dans l'espace public, consiste à simuler le décès de personnalités publiques pour générer des réactions émotionnelles fortes et faire grimper les statistiques de pages numériques peu scrupuleuses. Mais l'interprète de l'inspecteur Roch n'entend pas laisser cette dérive impunie. Prêt à appliquer dans le monde réel la rigueur de la loi qu'il feignait de faire respecter à la télévision, Sidibé Sékou Oumar a lancé un appel pour identifier le coupable : « Je serai reconnaissant pour qui arrive à repérer cet individu qui va répondre de ses actes. En attendant, qu'il soit au gnouf !!! » . En attendant que la lumière soit faite sur cette usurpation, l'artiste a tenu à saluer chaleureusement sa communauté et à exprimer sa profonde gratitude pour le soutien reçu : « Que Dieu nous donne longue vie dans la santé. Que Dieu nous bénisse toujours » . L'inspecteur Roch est bel et bien debout, et la traque numérique contre la désinformation, elle, ne fait que commencer. L’article Burkina Faso: Qui a « tué » l'inspecteur Rock de la série télévisée « Commissariat de Tampy » ? est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: La RS Berkane recrute l’international cap-verdien Ryan Mendes
items.description: La Renaissance sportive de Berkane (RSB) tient une nouvelle recrue d’expérience. Le club marocain a officiellement annoncé ce dimanche la signature de l’international cap-verdien Ryan Mendes, qui s’est engagé pour une saison avec une option de prolongation. Le contrat prévoit en effet une prolongation automatique d’une année supplémentaire si le joueur et le club atteignent les objectifs fixés en championnat national et en Ligue des champions de la CAF. À 36 ans, Ryan Mendes apporte toute son expérience à la formation berkanaise. L’attaquant cap-verdien s’est notamment illustré avec les Requins Bleus lors de la Coupe du monde 2026, avant de rejoindre le championnat marocain. Fort d’une longue carrière professionnelle, Mendes possède une expérience importante acquise aussi bien en Europe que dans les pays du Golfe. Son arrivée devrait permettre à la RSB de renforcer son secteur offensif avec un joueur habitué aux rendez-vous de haut niveau. Cette signature revêt également une dimension particulière pour Ryan Mendes puisqu’il va retrouver à Berkane son ancien sélectionneur avec le Cap-Vert, Pedro Leitão Brito, dit « Bubista ». Le technicien cap-verdien a récemment été nommé entraîneur principal de la Renaissance sportive de Berkane, en remplacement de Mouine Chaabani. La présence de Bubista pourrait ainsi faciliter l’intégration de Mendes dans son nouvel environnement et permettre au technicien de s’appuyer sur un joueur qu’il connaît parfaitement. La RSB se prépare à une saison ambitieuse, avec notamment la Ligue des champions de la CAF au programme. Le club berkani souhaite poursuivre sa dynamique et continuer à jouer les premiers rôles sur les scènes nationale et continentale. Avec l’arrivée de Ryan Mendes, Berkane mise donc sur l’expérience et la connaissance du haut niveau pour renforcer son effectif et atteindre ses objectifs cette saison. The post La RS Berkane recrute l’international cap-verdien Ryan Mendes appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Gestion des catastrophes et situations d’urgence : Le dispositif national de réponse mis à l’épreuve
items.description: Le ministère de l’Administration territoriale et de la Mobilité (MATM), à travers la Direction générale de la Protection civile (DGPC), la Brigade nationale de Sapeurs-Pompiers (BNSP) et le Secrétariat permanent du Conseil national de Secours d’Urgence et de Réhabilitation (SP/CONASUR), a organisé, le samedi 22 août 2026, à Ouagadougou, un exercice national de simulation de gestion de crise. Réalisé dans le cadre du déclenchement simulé du Plan d’Organisation des Secours (ORSEC) national, cet exercice vise à tester l’efficacité du dispositif national de réponse face à une catastrophe majeure, notamment en matière d’alerte, de coordination, de prise de décision et de déploiement des secours. Le scénario retenu reposait sur de fortes pluies ayant provoqué des inondations dans plusieurs localités. A Ouagadougou, le débordement des barrages n°2 et n°3 a entraîné l’inondation de zones d’habitation ainsi que la coupure de plusieurs voies d’accès. A cette situation, s’est ajouté un sinistre industriel à l’unité « RAMBO » de Kossodo, consécutif à une explosion suivie d’un incendie, faisant plusieurs blessés et brûlés et présentant des risques d’intoxication et de pollution des eaux. Face à l’ampleur de la crise simulée, le Plan ORSEC national a été déclenché à 9 h 30 mn au Centre de Veille, d’Alerte et de Coordination des Opérations de secours (COVACOS). Cette plateforme a permis de mettre à l’épreuve la chaîne de commandement, la circulation de l’information, la prise de décision et la coordination des interventions sur le terrain. L’exercice a mobilisé, aux côtés de la Direction générale de la Protection civile (DGPC), de la Brigade nationale de Sapeurs-Pompiers (BNSP), du Secrétariat permanent du Conseil national de Secours d’Urgence et de Réhabilitation (SP/CONASUR), la Police nationale, la Police municipale, les Eaux et Forêts, les services de santé, la Croix-Rouge ainsi que plusieurs autres structures intervenant dans la gestion des catastrophes. Sur le terrain, les équipes ont notamment simulé l’évacuation des populations, le secours et la prise en charge médicale des victimes, l’assistance aux personnes sinistrées ainsi que la coordination des différents acteurs engagés dans la réponse. A l’issue de la simulation, un point de situation a été présenté par le Directeur de la Réglementation et de la Prévention de la DGPC, le Camarade Capitaine Jean Charles TAMPANGA. Le bilan fictif établi fait état d’une victime décédée à la suite des inondations aux abords des barrages n°2 et n°3, de six (06) victimes en urgence absolue, 60 victimes en urgence relative et 100 personnes impliquées. Au-delà de la mise à l’épreuve du dispositif, l’exercice a permis d’identifier plusieurs axes d’amélioration. Il s’agit notamment du renforcement de la circulation de l’information entre les acteurs, de la réduction des délais de prise en charge des victimes, de l’anticipation de l’accueil des sinistrés, du renforcement des moyens logistiques en cas de crise prolongée et de l’amélioration de la communication avec les populations. Vingt (20) Officiers stagiaires venus du Rwanda, du Gabon et du Cameroun ont également pris part à l’exercice en qualité d’observateurs, dans le cadre de leur formation d’Officier de Compagnie. Représentant le Ministre d’Etat, Ministre de l’Administration territoriale et de la Mobilité, le Directeur de Cabinet par intérim, le Camarade Sibiri de Issa OUEDRAOGO, a salué la mobilisation et l’engagement des différents acteurs. Il a rappelé que le Plan ORSEC national est activé lorsque l’ampleur d’une catastrophe dépasse les capacités de réponse des niveaux territorial et régional. Il a également insisté sur l’importance de l’anticipation, de la coordination et de la préparation permanente pour assurer une réponse rapide et efficace. « La catastrophe ne prévient pas. Et comme la catastrophe ne prévient pas, il faut que nous soyons toujours en alerte pour qu’à chaque fois qu’il y aura une situation, nous soyons prêts à apporter la réponse », a- t -il souligné. A travers cet exercice, le ministère de l’Administration territoriale et de la Mobilité (MATM) a ainsi mis à l’épreuve l’ensemble de la chaîne nationale de gestion de crise, de l’alerte au déploiement des secours, en passant par la prise en charge médicale, l’assistance aux sinistrés et la coordination des interventions. Cette simulation grandeur nature constitue une étape importante dans le renforcement de la préparation collective et de la capacité des acteurs à agir vite, agir ensemble et protéger efficacement les populations face aux catastrophes et aux situations d’urgence. DCRP/MATM L’article Gestion des catastrophes et situations d’urgence : Le dispositif national de réponse mis à l’épreuve est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Enseignement supéreur: 1 800 diplômés orientés vers des études de master sur un total de 4 677 demandes
items.description: Le ministère de l'Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche scientifique a annoncé l'orientation de 1 800 diplômés de licence ayant obtenu d'excellents résultats vers des programmes de master en Mauritanie et à l'étranger, sur les 4 677 étudiants ayant déposé une demande pour poursuivre leurs études. Par ailleurs, chaque médecin généraliste dont le dossier était complet s'est vu attribuer une place pour suivre une spécialisation médicale en Algérie ou au Maroc, selon le communiqué du ministère. Le ministère a précisé que le nombre de diplômés de licence cette année s’élevait à 5 871 étudiants répartis dans 108 formations nationales, et que 4 677 étudiants avaient demandé à poursuivre leurs études en master. Le processus d’orientation a concerné 1 237 étudiants vers 62 programmes de master en Mauritanie, contre 563 étudiants vers des programmes à l’étranger, ce qui représente environ 31 % du nombre total de diplômés de licence et 38 % du nombre total de demandes d’admission en master. Le ministère a ajouté avoir réservé 20 places à la mobilité internationale, notamment dans les domaines de la physique et de l’ingénierie. Dans le domaine de la médecine, le ministère a indiqué avoir orienté 194 médecins généralistes vers des programmes de résidence médicale en Algérie et au Maroc, répartis sur 45 spécialités, soit 144 places en Algérie et 50 au Maroc. Il a précisé que chaque médecin généraliste dont le dossier était complet avait eu la possibilité d’intégrer un internat, à condition que cela n’entre pas en conflit avec ses obligations nationales liées au travail ou à l’internat. Le ministère prévoit de rouvrir la plateforme d’orientation le mercredi 26 août pour les lauréats de la deuxième session, ainsi que pour les lauréats de l’année dernière souhaitant changer d’orientation. Le ministère a précisé que cette même période offrira une seconde chance aux lauréats de la première session qui n’ont pas participé à la première phase d’orientation, afin qu’ils puissent rattraper leur retard.

items.title: Australia see spike in near-misses amid air traffic controller shortage
items.description: Australia’s shortage of air traffic controllers is showing signs of nearing a breaking point after the country’s busiest airport recorded at least four near misses in the past month. Since late July, incidents at Sydney Airport included a passenger jet aborting its take-off because there was a plane in its path. In a separate close call, an aircraft that was taxiing had to slam on the brakes to avoid colliding with another jet. Short-staffed control towers have long been a problem globally, but...

items.title: 36 mois de prison dont 12 ferme requis contre une exciseuse : le TGI Ouaga I durcit le ton contre les mutilations génitales
items.description: La chambre correctionnelle du TGI Ouaga I a examiné, le vendredi 21 août 2026, une affaire de mutilations génitales féminines impliquant six prévenues. Fatou (nom d’emprunt), accusée d’avoir pratiqué les excisions, comparaissait aux côtés de cinq femmes poursuivies pour complicité. Les faits concernent trois fillettes, âgées de 7 à 10 ans. Selon les débats, les excisions ont été organisées le 14 juillet 2026 à Bissighin, à l’initiative de Rachelle (nom d’emprunt), avec l’intervention de l’exciseuse Fatou. Oumou, Fanta et Clémence (tous des noms d’emprunts) ont facilité l’opération, tandis que Minata (nom d’emprunt), mère de l’une des victimes, affirme avoir découvert les faits à son retour. Une seule lame aurait servi aux trois excisions, pour lesquelles l’exciseuse aurait reçu 30 000 FCFA. À la barre, les prévenues ont reconnu les faits, tout en affirmant ignorer leur caractère illégal et en sollicitant la clémence du tribunal. Les parents des victimes ne se sont pas constitués partie civile, mais ont déploré les actes commis. Le parquet a requis 36 mois d’emprisonnement, dont 12 mois ferme, et 500 000 FCFA d’amende ferme contre Fatou. Il a également requis, contre Rachelle, Oumou, Fanta et Clémence, 36 mois de prison dont 8 mois ferme et 500 000 FCFA d’amende. La relaxe de Minata a été demandée pour infraction non constituée. La défense a plaidé la clémence et le sursis. Le verdict est attendu le 29 août 2026. items.title: Unlearnt lessons of history
items.description: TODAY, the country’s hybrid government is fixated on altering Pakistan’s constitutionally mandated provincial structure and multiplying administrative units. To sell the idea, establishment apologists have rolled out some disingenuous arguments. They claim this will improve governance and miraculously solve the country’s problems overnight. A debate has been generated in the media about the pros and cons of administrative changes and breaking provinces into more units. Parliament has yet to discuss this. That is unsurprising. Deliberation is not this legislature’s strong suit. It has rushed through constitutional amendments in record time, once in the dead of night and without meaningful debate. Meanwhile, speculation is mounting that another constitutional amendment is being prepared to push through ‘administrative changes’. Absent from the establishment’s consideration of these sweeping changes are lessons from Pakistan’s history. Over the decades, the country’s rulers have experimented with parliamentary, presidential, semi-presidential, quasi-parliamentary systems, direct military rule, and more recently a hybrid model, which involves informal power-sharing between the military and civilians, with the former as dominant partner. Pakistan has tried them all. Yet each switch only contributed to political instability. The only system to command legitimacy and broad support is parliamentary democracy, despite the fact that parliamentary supremacy over the executive has never been realised. Linked to these experiments has been the status and rights of provinces in a federal system. As the provincial configuration and federating units largely coincided with the ethnic composition of people of each province, the need was always felt to make federalism a reality, not just a constitutional precept to ensure the people of all four provinces felt they were part of an inclusive and fair system. Pakistan’s troubled history offers a cautionary lesson against altering the provincial structure. But the federal structure and provincial rights have always been contested issues in Pakistan’s history. Contested on many counts. Smaller provinces have long resented Punjab’s political hegemony, sought greater powers and autonomy and felt the distribution of resources has been unfair. Unelected institutions have always preferred a centralised polity while military rule meant the country functioned as a virtual unitary state. Long periods of unrepresentative rule fuelled alienation among the smaller provinces by marginalising them, suppressing regional identities, concentrating power at the centre and weakening federalism. The creation of One Unit in the 1950s, which merged all the provinces of what was then West Pakistan into a single unit, was aimed at creating ‘parity’ with the more populous eastern wing of the country to undercut its numerical majority. This politically motivated project imposed a unitary system and all but destroyed the country’s federal character. It was justified by totally false and frivolous arguments. They included claims it would end “provincial prejudices”, reduce adm­i­nistrative expenses and help develop backward areas. The move had disastrous consequences. It fanned the flames of nationalist and regionalist sentiment in the smaller provinces of West Pak­istan and strengthened centrifugal forces across the country. It contributed to the sense of discrimination among the people of East Pakistan that, along with other factors, found expression in the Bengali nationalist movement and ultimately led to the break-up of Pakistan in 1971. The issue of provincial rights continued to be a source of tensions and contestation. The 1973 Constitution struck a delicate balance between the centre and provinces in a multiethnic state, assured provincial autonomy and enjoined reciprocal obligations between the federating units. Unfortunately, this was observed more in its breach than in its adherence. Opposition-run provincial governments were ousted in the 1970s by prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto. This reinforced a political tradition that began in the early years after independence when provincial governments were summarily dismissed by the central government. This seriously undermined national unity. These and other actions widened interprovincial disparities, deepened alienation among smaller provinces and led to the insurgency in Balochistan in the 1970s. This intensified during the 2000s but their antecedents reached back to the 1950s. The insurgency continues today as a result of monumental mishandling of the province and Baloch sentiment by successive governments. Authoritarian measures also gave a fillip to Pakhtun nationalism, even though over time this waned with the increasing representation of KP in the country’s power elite and bure­aucracy. The troubled history of federalism and provincial tensions in Pakistan offers a cautionary lesson against altering the country’s four ethnically distinct provinces. Past attempts to do that or erode constitutionally guaranteed provincial rights only widened fault lines and created new ones. These efforts were never about better governance or a stronger administrative system. They were about control. They reflected the interests of a ruling elite seeking to entrench political dominance, with little regard for national unity and cohesion. The same logic applies to those in the current hybrid government pushing to create new provinces and fragment existing ones. This is about control, not reform. True ethnic minorities in some provinces, such as Seraiki speakers in southern Punjab, have long wanted their own province. Some political parties have actively supported this. But the challenge is how to square this with carving out a new unit that could undermine the delicate constitutional balance, spark controversy and encourage others to demand new provinces. The 18th Constitutional Amendment , backed by all parties in 2010, opened a new chapter in provincial empowerment. Over a dozen ministries were devolved from the federal level to the provinces. But this also raised capacity issues and whether provinces could handle the increased fiscal power and resources devolved to them. The fiscal aspect evoked the most criticism. Because with the 2009 National Finance Commission award, the substantial transfer of resources to the provinces left the federal government unable to meet its financial obligations. While this tussle over revenue needs to be resolved and provinces should mobilise their own resources, creating smaller provinces or rolling back the amendment is not the answer. In fact, the rationale for redrawing provincial boundaries remains opaque. This lack of clarity reinforces the impression that the motive is to increase control, not to improve governance. If we want real reform, it’s not by carving out new provinces. It’s by empowering local government. The writer is a former ambassador to the US, UK and UN. Published in Dawn, August 24th, 2026

items.title: Un groupe électrogène en provenance du Sénégal pour aider au rétablissement de l’électricité à Nouakchott
items.description: Un groupe électrogène est arrivé dimanche soir à Rosso, en vue de son transfert vers Nouakchott afin de contribuer au rétablissement de l'approvisionnement en électricité après deux incendies qui ont ravagé deux postes de transformation de la capitale en l'espace de deux jours, selon une source de « Sahara Media ». Le correspondant de « Sahara Media » à Rosso a indiqué que le groupe électrogène était arrivé dimanche soir en provenance du Sénégal et qu’il avait quitté la ville en direction de Nouakchott au sein d’un convoi composé de techniciens et escorté par une unité de la gendarmerie. Le groupe électrogène doit être acheminé vers l’une des deux sous-stations endommagées par l’incendie, dans le cadre des efforts en cours visant à renforcer le réseau électrique et à accélérer le rétablissement du service dans les quartiers qui subissent encore des coupures. Un incendie s’était déclaré dans la sous-station de l’Est, au nord de Nouakchott, avant qu’une autre sous-station de 33/15 kV, située à l’ouest de Nouakchott, ne soit touchée par un autre incendie, provoquant d’importantes coupures d’électricité dans la capitale. La Société mauritanienne d’électricité (Somelec) a indiqué dans son dernier communiqué que ses équipes techniques avaient remis en service la ligne Nouakchott-Idini, qui alimente les puits d’eau potable, et rétabli l’électricité dans d’autres zones grâce à des lignes d’alimentation parallèles et de remplacement. La société a ajouté que de vastes zones de l’ouest de Nouakchott ont commencé à retrouver progressivement l’électricité dimanche soir, en fonction des capacités de charge disponibles sur le réseau, tandis que ses équipes poursuivent la réparation des parties endommagées des cellules de distribution et des disjoncteurs, ainsi que le rétablissement du service dans les autres zones.

items.title: Outgoing Saudi envoy meets president
items.description: Saudi Ambassador Nawaf bin Said Al-Malki calls on President Asif Ali Zardari at Aiwan-i-Sadr.—APP ISLAMABAD: President Asif Ali Zardari on Sunday appreciated the contribution of Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to Pakistan Nawaf bin Said Al-Malki towards strengthening the longstanding fraternal and strategic bilateral ties. Ambassador Malki, who has served in Pakistan since 2017, called on the president for a farewell call at Aiwan-i-Sadr. President Zardari expressed appreciation for his dedicated service and the friendship, warmth and cooperation he extended to Pakistan during his tenure. He said the ambassador had played an important role in advancing bilateral relations, particularly in the political, economic and trade spheres. Pakistan deeply values its time-tested friendship and strategic partnership with Saudi Arabia and appreciated the Kingdom’s steadfast support for Pakistan, he said. items.title: Le président mauritanien ordonne au gouvernement de déterminer les causes des pannes électriques dans la capitale et d’en déterminer les responsabilités
items.description: Le président mauritanien Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani a ordonné de déterminer les causes des pannes qui ont touché deux postes de transformation électrique à Nouakchott et d’établir les responsabilités, tout en accordant la priorité au rétablissement du service électrique dans les plus brefs délais, après les coupures généralisées subies par la capitale au cours des deux derniers jours. Dans une déclaration faite à l’issue de sa visite sur l’une des deux sous-stations endommagées, Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani a indiqué avoir donné des instructions « afin de déterminer les causes de ces incidents, d’établir les responsabilités et de prendre toutes les mesures nécessaires pour éviter que de telles pannes ne se reproduisent à l’avenir ». Le président a ajouté qu’il avait chargé le gouvernement de mobiliser tous les moyens humains, techniques et matériels nécessaires et d’accélérer le rythme des interventions, tout en respectant strictement les normes de sécurité et de sûreté. Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani a précisé que la sous-station de l’Est avait repris son fonctionnement, tandis qu’une « solution d’urgence » était mise en œuvre dans la sous-station du Nord afin de la remettre en service dans les plus brefs délais. Les déclarations du président font suite à deux incendies qui ont ravagé vendredi et samedi deux postes de transformation à Nouakchott, provoquant de graves perturbations dans l’approvisionnement en électricité de la capitale et des coupures de courant dans plusieurs quartiers et zones. La Société mauritanienne d’électricité (Somelec) avait annoncé le rétablissement progressif de l’électricité dans plusieurs zones grâce à des lignes d’alimentation de secours, ainsi que la remise en service de la ligne Nouakchott-Idini qui alimente les puits d’eau potable. Le président a insisté sur la nécessité de poursuivre et d’accélérer les efforts visant à moderniser le réseau de distribution d’électricité à Nouakchott, alors que les équipes techniques poursuivent les travaux de réparation des parties endommagées et rétablissent le service dans les zones encore touchées par les coupures.

items.title: Jamaat threatens march on Islamabad over petroleum levy
items.description: • Hafiz Naeem says sit-ins to be converted into shutter-down strike on 13th Rabiul Awwal • Party to stage indefinite protest outside Governor House in Quetta from 29th LAHORE / KARACHI: Jamaat-i-Islami chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman on Sunday warned the government that the party would expand its ongoing sit-ins into a nationwide movement, culminating in a shutter-down strike and a possible march on Islamabad if the petroleum levy was not withdrawn. Addressing a press conference at the JI sit-in site in Lahore, Mr Rehman said the protests in the provincial capital had entered their eighth day and would continue until the government abolished the petroleum levy. He announced that JI would establish protest camps across the country and call a nationwide shutter-down strike on 13th Rabiul Awwal, followed by a march towards Islamabad if the government failed to respond to its demands. “The rulers are squeezing the blood out of the people through forced levies and taxes,” he said, adding that the government was protecting the privileges of the ruling elite while shifting the burden of its policies onto ordinary citizens. Mr Rehman said public pressure had forced the government to reduce the price of diesel by Rs32 per litre. He said oil mafias had been making excessive profits by charging consumers for imported diesel at rates linked to the cost of locally produced diesel. The JI chief also said the government and sugar mafia were manipulating the sugar market. He said 765,000 tonnes of sugar had been imported in collusion with vested interests without taxes, yet sugar prices continued to rise. He announced that JI would celebrate Eid Miladun Nabi on 12th Rabiul Awwal at the sit-in sites. Series of sit-ins According to a statement issued by the JI from Islamabad, the party announced a series of protest sit-ins across the federal capital as part of its nationwide protest campaign against the petroleum levy, rising fuel prices, inflation and costly agreements with independent power producers. A protest sit-in was staged in the federal capital’s Ghori Town on Sunday. Another sit-in will be staged in Islamabad’s Karachi Company today (Monday), followed by protests in Sector G-7/3 on 25th, B-17 on 27th and the PWD neighbourhood on 28th. The next demonstrations will be held on Aug 29, 30 and 31 in Bharakahu, Jhangi Syedan and Lehtrar Road, respectively. ‘PPP conniving with PML-N’ In Karachi, the JI’s sit-in near Governor House continued for the eighth consecutive day on Sunday, with party leaders insisting that the protest would not be called off unless the government withdrew the petroleum levy and provided relief to consumers. Addressing the protesters, JI Karachi chief Monem Zafar Khan said the party would continue its struggle until the petroleum levy was withdrawn. He maintained that the levy had placed an additional burden on ordinary citizens already struggling with inflation and high utility bills. He also criticised the Sindh government, accusing it of “conniving” with the PML-N-led federal government instead of protecting the interests of people. Meanwhile, the JI Balochistan announced plans to stage an indefinite sit-in outside Governor House in Quetta starting from Aug 29. The protest aims to challenge unfulfilled government promises, high petroleum levy, and rising lawlessness. Speaking at a press conference at the Quetta Press Club, JI Provincial Vice President Zahid Akhtar Baloch said the sit-in would continue until the party’s demands were met. With additional input from Bakhtawar Mian in Islamabad and Muhammad Akbar Notezai in Quetta Published in Dawn, August 24th, 2026

items.title: Women’s leadership
items.description: PAKISTAN doesn’t fare well on indices related to gender gap and women’s empowerment. The damning statistics include the number of girls who are out of school, the wide gender digital divide, high rates of violence against women, and women’s low representation in private and public leadership positions. However, over time, there have been significant advances for Pakistani women leaders. Mohammad Ali Jinnah’s sister, Fatima Jinnah , was a key figure in Pakistan’s independence movement. She later became a presidential candidate, derided by the dictator Gen Ayub Khan. When Benazir Bhutto was elected prime minister in 1988, Pakistan became the first Muslim-majority country to be led by a woman. Pakistani women have led movements against dictators, including generals Ayub, Zia and Musharraf. Asma Jahangir was the first woman to be elected president of the Supreme Court Bar Association. Begum Naseem Wali Khan was the first woman to win a general election seat in the country. Justice Ayesha Malik is the first woman Supreme Court judge. Currently, Maryam Nawaz is the first woman chief minister in Pakistan. Trans women have also made their mark, with Aisha Mughal being the first to represent a country at a UN session. Recently, Nayyab Ali was nominated for a civilian award by the government. But despite these significant positives, the prosecution of political women in Pakistan is at an all-time high. Several women leaders of the PTI remain behind bars, including the ageing cancer survivor, Dr Yasmin Rashid, who has health issues . Since January, award-winning human rights lawyer Imaan Mazari Hazir has been in jail serving a 17-year sentence for mere tweets. Baloch women have now joined numerous men who have been forcibly disappeared; several remain in jail in politically motivated cases. The prosecution of political women in the country is at an all-time high. Do such incarcerations, cases and disappearances send an encouraging message to young girls across Pakistan? Does it motivate reluctant families to send girls to school so they can get an education and start careers? Does it motivate young lawyers to take up cases of the voiceless pro bono? Does it encourage young women to enter politics and do good for the people? The incarcerations reflect a deep-rooted patriarchy that plagues the entire system. Take, for instance, gender-based attacks against women during election campaigns. The Digital Rights Foundation documented at least 163 social media posts in the run-up to the 2024 election that included gendered disinformation against women politicians, and at least 47 posts targeting “journalists covering the elections, subjecting them to gendered insults and online trolling campaigns that included online threats of physical assault”. Deepfakes targeting women human rights defenders have become commonplace, with dehumanising content being disseminated online of women that are critical of state policies, with little to no consequences for such actions — despite Section 22 of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act that makes edited and non-consensual imagery a crime. Since the 2025 amendment to Peca , the state is an eager complainant against journalists who are critical of it. Whereas the new ability of the state to file cybercrime cases against activists, journalists and politicians is to be condemned and should be reversed; it is worth noting that the state doesn’t take cognisance of instances of harassment and vitriol on social media that lead to crimes against women and children. This includes routine cases of men mercilessly killing women for rejecting their advances and proposals. The victims include women who are public figures on social media platforms as content creators. On Aug 20, former professor and motivational speaker Faisal Asghar Imam was named in the murder case of his wife in their home, and social media was rife with testimonies of him making his students uncomfortable in class and online. The link between online misogyny and physical harm to life must not be taken lightly. When Peca was being promulgated, those of us who opposed it were labelled anti-women for opposing the law. Today, we see how women are harassed, jailed, and punished including for naming their harassers by the same law meant to protect them. The abuse of the law is not restricted to targeting women who dare to speak truth to power. Human rights lawyer Hadi Ali Chattha is currently serving a 17-year sentence for supporting his wife Imaan Mazari Hazir, with his punishment framed for the “crime” of reposting her tweets. Seemingly, men who support women related to them, they too will be punished. In our geopolitical context, targeting women in the public sphere is particularly alarming. Girls in Afghanistan are not allowed to go to school after Class 6; women are not allowed to leave their house for employment, and they cannot even sing or be heard in public. In Iran, women have been killed for simply opposing the state’s enforcement of head covering rules. In such an environment, it would be a powerful message to the neighbourhood if Pakistan has women in positions of power. Sadly, the current women’s leadership in Pakistan is hardly representative of half the population. There are no women federal ministers, and only one woman minister of state. In Sindh, the PPP that brought us a woman prime minister has only two women cabinet members; while the party’s cabinet in Balochistan has only one woman minister. In KP, the PTI has no women in the cabinet. A woman chief minister leads Punjab, but her cabinet has only two women ministers, with Marriyum Aurangzeb holding six portfolios. As a pluralist federal democracy, at least on paper, Pakistan must move in line with Article 25 of the Constitution that empowers the government to make special provisions to protect women and children, apart from ensuring equal treatment for them. Women political prisoners, along with men, must be released; and women being half the population must be given half of the governing share. We owe this to every young girl in Pakistan. The writer is director of Bolo Bhi, an advocacy forum for digital rights. X: @UsamaKhilji Published in Dawn, August 24th, 2026

items.title: Oil falls ahead of US announcement on new Iran sanctions
items.description: Oil prices slipped more than $1 a barrel on Monday as investors took ‌profits ahead of an expected announcement from Washington about imposing more sanctions on Iran that may further disrupt supplies from the Middle East. Brent crude futures fell $1.22, or 1.29%, to $93.17 by 0035 GMT, while ​U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude was at $85.86 a barrel, down $1.20, or 1.38%. Both contracts posted their second weekly gains last week, up more than 5%, as peace talks between the U.S. and Iran hit a stalemate, capping oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, where a fifth of the world’s supply used to transit. U.S. Treasury ​Secretary Scott Bessent , set to hold a press conference at 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT) on Monday, has threatened to impose “the toughest sanctions in history” on Iran. President Donald Trump has also threatened to ​impose sanctions on Iran’s trading partners. “It is unclear whether U.S. policy to economically isolate ​Iran will prove effective,” Vivek Dhar, a commodities analyst at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, wrote in ‌a note. “But if the U.S. measures do work as intended, Iran’s ability to respond via increased violence becomes a growing risk for energy markets to consider.” Iran has condemned U.S. plans to announce new sanctions even as President Masoud Pezeshkian called for a diplomatic solution . “The more ​pragmatic members of ​the Iranian leadership would ⁠prefer to de-escalate, but the hardliners would probably prefer to fight to the bitter end,” IG markets analyst Tony Sycamore said. “I ​think by the end of this week we will have ​a good ⁠idea which side of the Iranian leadership has the upper hand.” Offers of Iranian crude to Chinese buyers have declined , and prices have jumped as the U.S. blockade has cut Tehran’s shipments, ⁠according ​to trade sources. However, Iran has granted permission for a ​number of Iraqi oil tankers to pass through the Strait following repeated requests from Baghdad, Iran’s state news ​agency IRNA reported on Saturday.

items.title: ‘Grand dialogue’
items.description: THE country’s top civil and military leaders are absolutely right when they say that dialogue and development are needed to address Balochistan’s crises. But perhaps one should recall that many earlier attempts by the state to bring peace to the province were stalled or remain unimplemented. In order to truly stabilise Balochistan and bring lasting peace to this troubled province, a credible political process must begin, with the state guaranteeing that it will fully implement previous promises, as well as new agreements. While speaking at the Balochistan National Workshop in Islamabad recently, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif called for a “grand, frank and meaningful dialogue” to address the province’s issues. He added that the province’s people had first right over its resources. In a similar vein the chief of defence forces stressed the need for empowering Balochistan’s youth. It is certainly welcome that the rulers see the need to tackle Balochistan’s political problems through dialogue. While kinetic measures are needed to deal with immediate terrorist threats, the underlying factors fuelling discontent can only be handled through a political process. The state must keep in mind previous attempts to address the province’s problems. For example, the PPP government had in 2009 launched the Aghaz-i-Huqooq-i-Balochistan package. Despite the passage of 17 years, many of the package’s key points remain unimplemented. For example, it had proposed releasing political workers, except those involved in heinous crimes. However, over the past few months, we have seen peaceful activists rounded up and thrown in jail. Similarly, the 2009 package had sought to address the province’s socioeconomic woes; suffice it to say, social indicators in Balochistan remain miserable. The PML-N had launched a package of its own in 2015. Much of that scheme also remains unfulfilled. CPEC was similarly supposed to transform the province’s fortunes. It has not. Instead of reinventing the wheel, the state must implement what it had promised in these packages. Many of these schemes’ salient points reflect the demands of the province’s nationalist politicians. Therefore, to implement these promises in full, a grand dialogue should bring on board the province’s genuine political leadership, as well as peaceful activists, while a verifiable and transparent mechanism needs to be worked out to help implement previous and new promises. The past few months have seen a sharp spike in terrorist activity in Balochistan . The only sustainable way of addressing the insurgency is to supplement kinetic actions with a genuine political process that can, in the long-term, eliminate the underlying factors that are fuelling discontent. Published in Dawn, August 24th, 2026

items.title: South Africa’s former world boxing champion Tete shot dead outside his home
items.description: Former world boxing champion Zolani “Last Born” Tete was shot dead outside his ​home in South Africa’s Eastern Cape province ‌on Friday, police and the country’s sports minister said. The 38-year-old was arriving at his residence in Mdantsane township when ​two armed men wearing balaclavas got out ​of a vehicle and opened fire. The Reuters Inside Track newsletter is your essential guide to global sports news. Sign up here. “I will not ⁠speculate about who did this or why,” ​Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie said in a statement. Tete’s killing ​will renew attention on violent crime in South Africa, which continues to have one of the world’s highest murder rates ​despite recent declines in homicides. The murder ​of the world champion has also struck a chord in Mdantsane, ‌the ⁠Eastern Cape township that has produced some of South Africa’s most successful boxers. A 27-year-old woman travelling with Tete was shot multiple times and taken ​to hospital. Police ​have started ⁠investigations and the motive remains unclear. Tete won the IBF junior-bantamweight world title ​in 2014 after defeating Japan’s Teiru Kinoshita ​in ⁠Kobe. He later won the WBO bantamweight crown. He is best remembered internationally for his 11-second knockout of ⁠fellow ​South African Siboniso Gonya in ​Belfast in November 2017, the fastest stoppage in a world title ​fight.

items.title: L’Ordre des Médecins du Burkina en deuil: Décès du du Dr Boinzemwendé Jean Arnaud Koudougou à 35 ans
items.description: Le Conseil National de l’Ordre des Médecins du Burkina Faso (CNOM-BF) est plongé dans l’affliction. L’institution a annoncé le décès du Docteur Boinzemwendé Jean Arnaud KOUDOUGOU, survenu le jeudi 20 août 2026 au CHU Yalgado Ouédraogo. Âgé de seulement 35 ans, ce médecin en cours de spécialisation d'ophtalmologie s'est éteint des suites d'une courte maladie, laissant derrière lui une corporation médicale profondément endeuillée. La communauté médicale burkinabè fait face à une douloureuse perte. À travers le communiqué nécrologique n° 012/2026, le Conseil National de l’Ordre des Médecins du Burkina Faso (CNOM-BF) a partagé la triste nouvelle de la disparition de l’un de ses membres, le Docteur Boinzemwendé Jean Arnaud KOUDOUGOU. Le jeune médecin s'est éteint le jeudi 20 août 2026 au Centre Hospitalier Universitaire (CHU) Yalgado Ouédraogo, succombant à une courte maladie. Le Dr Koudougou est parti à l'aube de sa carrière, dans sa 36e année de vie. Professionnel dévoué, il s'était engagé dans un parcours d'excellence en poursuivant sa troisième année de spécialisation en Ophtalmologie. Officiellement reconnu par l’institution de régulation nationale, il était inscrit à l’Ordre National des Médecins du Burkina Faso sous le numéro 4044 (CROM OUAGA). Sa disparition représente une perte regrettable pour le corps médical, qui voit s'éteindre un futur spécialiste prometteur. L'annonce de son décès a suscité une vive vague d'émotion et de recueillement. Au nom de l'ensemble de la grande famille des médecins du Burkina Faso, le Président du CNOM-BF, le Dr Abdoul-Guaniyi SAWADOGO, a exprimé sa profonde compassion. Il a adressé ses condoléances les plus sincères à la famille biologique du défunt, ainsi qu’à ses proches et à tous ses collaborateurs de terrain. Dans un appel à l'union de prière, le président de l’Ordre a émis le vœu solennel que l'âme de leur regretté camarade repose en paix. Les hommages continuent d'affluer au sein de la corporation pour saluer la mémoire d’un confrère estimé et regretter un départ bien trop prématuré. items.title: Fast-moving wildfire in Nevada injures 6, forces 42,000 to evacuate
items.description: Authorities in the United States said on Sunday that at least six people were injured and 42,000 were ordered to evacuate as a fast-moving wildfire spread rapidly toward Reno, a city in northwestern Nevada near the Nevada-California border. The Hawk Fire, which began on Saturday, has grown to more than 53 square kilometers so far and remained completely uncontained, fire officials said at a news conference on Sunday. Officials added that the injured included three civilians and three first responders, and an additional 45,000 people were in the evacuation warning zone. They also confirmed that several structures have been destroyed in the fire. About 10,000 customers were without power in Washoe County on Sunday. Reno is the county seat and most populous city of Washoe County. Officials said that extreme fire behavior has been observed, with wind-driven fire making significant runs through light, flashy fuels. Nevada Governor Joe Lombardo declared a state of emergency for Washoe County on Saturday night. "This is an active and rapidly evolving situation, and I urge everyone in the affected areas to remain vigilant and follow the direction of local officials," Lombardo said in a statement. "The state is fully engaged, and we are working alongside local authorities and first responders to deploy every available resource to protect lives, safeguard communities, and keep Nevadans out of harm's way." The governor warned again on Sunday morning on social media that the fire is still "a rapidly evolving situation." "Stay vigilant and keep yourself informed if you are in the affected areas," the governor said.

items.title: Banwa/Tansila : Un enfant perd la vie après avoir reçu un coup de bâton destiné à sa mère
items.description: Un enfant a trouvé la mort le vendredi 21 août 2026 à Orowé, dans la commune de Tansila, après avoir été atteint par un coup de bâton porté par son père contre sa mère lors d’une dispute conjugale, a appris l’AIB. Selon les informations recueillies sur place, l’incident est survenu à la suite d’une dispute entre un homme et son épouse. Emporté par la colère, l’homme aurait tenté de frapper sa femme à l’aide d’un bâton. Pour éviter le coup, celle-ci aurait esquivé le bâton qui a malheureusement atteint l’enfant qui se trouvait à proximité. Grièvement touché, l’enfant a été rapidement conduit au Centre de santé et de promotion sociale (CSPS) de la localité. Il a cependant succombé à ses blessures quelques instants après son admission. Le drame s’est produit dans le village d’Orowé, situé à environ 10 km de Tansila, chef-lieu de la commune, et à 45 km de Solenzo. L’incident rappelle les conséquences parfois dramatiques des violences au sein des familles. items.title: Bobo-Dioulasso : Deux filles se battent violemment pour « une affaire de garçon »
items.description: Une scène d'une rare violence a opposé deux jeunes filles dans la ville de Bobo-Dioulasso, à la suite d'un différend sentimental lié à un garçon. Selon les faits rapportés sur les réseau sociaux, cette altercation verbale a rapidement basculé dans l’affrontement physique, l’une des protagonistes menaçant désormais de porter l'affaire devant les autorités judiciaires. Ce fait divers, qui met en lumière les dérives de la violence chez les jeunes, pose la question cruciale du rôle des familles et de l'éducation à la maîtrise de soi au sein de la société. La capitale économique du Burkina Faso, Bobo-Dioulasso, a été le théâtre d’un incident qui suscite de nombreuses interrogations et l'indignation générale. D'après les informations partagées sur Facebook, une dispute violente a éclaté entre deux jeunes filles, ayant pour unique point de discorde une rivalité autour d'un garçon. Ce qui n'était au départ qu'un échange d'invectives verbales a rapidement échappé à tout contrôle. Selon les propos et les échanges entendus sur les lieux de l'altercation, la tension est montée d'un cran lorsque les injures réciproques ont dégénéré en une véritable bastonnade. L’affrontement physique a été d’une telle intensité que l’une des deux jeunes filles, physiquement malmenée, a ouvertement déclaré son intention d'engager des poursuites. Elle a ainsi affirmé qu’elle allait chercher une convocation officielle à l’encontre de celle qui l’a battue. Face à la futilité apparente du motif de cette altercation — se battre physiquement pour un homme —, la question de l'éducation se pose avec acuité. Cette dérive comportementale souligne un besoin urgent d'encadrement au sein du cercle familial. Les parents ont, à cet égard, un rôle fondamental à assumer auprès de leurs enfants. Il leur appartient de s’impliquer activement en prenant le temps de les écouter et de les conseiller sur les valeurs essentielles du respect d'autrui, de la maîtrise de soi, de la saine gestion des relations amoureuses et des conséquences souvent destructrices de la violence. Cet incident physique va directement à l'encontre des valeurs collectives promues au Burkina Faso. Comme le rappelle le cadre idéologique de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire, le pays doit s'appuyer sur des principes cardinaux tels que le vivre-ensemble, la cohésion sociale et le travail. Dans cette perspective de construction nationale, la patrie a un besoin impérieux de travailleurs dévoués et de bâtisseurs d’avenir, et non de citoyens prompts à se bagarrer. L’article Bobo-Dioulasso : Deux filles se battent violemment pour « une affaire de garçon » est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Fazl blames lack of joint opposition for unchecked legislation
items.description: JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman addresses a workers’ convention in Peshawar.—PPI PESHAWAR: JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman on Sunday pointed out a structural weakness on opposition benches, noting that the opposition leader failed to unite parties to effectively challenge the recent government legislation on armed forces command. While noting that opposition walkouts without act­ive resistance have harmed democratic checks and balances, the JUI-F chief urged joint opposition coordination inside parliament to prevent further unche­cked legislative actions. “The recent legislation was passed in a great haste, without any debate and even opposition members did not examine it in detail,” Maulana Fazl added while addressing party workers’ convention, organised by the JUI-F Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chapter, in Peshawar. In his speech, he offered scathing critique of the recent legislations, creation of new provinces and law and order situation in the country. Calls new provinces move ‘a tactic’ to roll back NFC Award He said that they supported Pakistan’s strong defence capability, but rejected military’s interference in politics. Maulana Fazl regretted that even the administrative powers of prime minister within the armed forces have now been vested in one person. He noted the laws also had an overriding effect over other legislations that were in conflict with it. He claimed that when they had raised in parliament the issue of making the Holy Quran and Sunnah as the supreme law of the land in the past, the then chief justice of Pakistan declared that all clauses of the Constitution were equal and no single clause could be superior to another. However, he said that legislation was carried out to concentrate power and authority in establishment with overriding effect over other laws that were in conflict with it. The powers that should have been vested in parliament were concentrated within a person, he reiterated, adding that his office’s authority had been extended over the army, air force, and the navy as well and it would hold all powers, including dismissing someone, extending someone’s service, accepting and rejecting someone resignation, and all these powers were previously vested in the federal government. He said that the wishes of the head of one institution were being imposed on all other institutions and the entire nation. Maulana Fazl said that as the federal government surrendered its authority and it could also enact any other legislation whenever need arises, taking the parliament out of the equation. He said that it was the opposition leader’s job to unite all the parties sitting on opposition benches and it was lacking there. He said he met the opposition leader and discussed a joint strategy to play their role as joint opposition inside the parliament. He said he has proposed to the opposition leader to keep an eye on such things inside the parliament. “They have done a big damage and we do not even know what has happened,” he said. He also said that the same law immediately went to Senate and passed within 30 minutes and the opposition was happy about staging a walkout. The JUI-F chief underscored the importance of a strong opposition in parliament to force the government to listen to them. New provinces Referring to the security situation in KP, Maulana Fazl also criticised the formation of new provinces, saying that it was not prudent to talk about divisions when the house itself was on fire. He believed the creation of new provinces was aimed at reversing the National Finance Commission Award and “capturing” the mineral resources of provinces. He recalled that they had also opposed the Fata merger with KP and the situation vindicated their stance. Published in Dawn, August 24th, 2026
